tb-408-1.question:
Why is a closed iron core used in a transformer?

(1) It reduces eddy currents.

(2) It reduces magnetic flux leakage.

(3) It allows current to flow from the primary coil to the secondary coil through it.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-408-1.reasoning:
A closed iron core does not reduce eddy currents. Eddy currents can be reduced by using a laminated core.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

A closed iron core traps the magnetic field in closed loops to reduce flux leakage.

∴ (2) is correct.

Current in the primary coil does not flow to the secondary coil.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-408-3.question:
Which of the following statements about the transmission of electricity is/are correct?

(1) The longer the distance of transmission, the higher the power loss.

(2) The longer the length of the transmission cables, the greater the resistance of the cable per km.

(3) The higher the voltage of transmission, the greater the voltage drop in the cables.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-408-3.reasoning:
A longer transmission cable has a higher resistance. Therefore, the power loss is higher.

∴ (1) is correct.

The resistance of the cable per km depends only on the material and thickness of the cable.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

By P = VI, a smaller current I flows through the transmission cables if electricity is transmitted at a higher voltage V. Therefore, the voltage drop (= IR) in the cables is smaller.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-408-8.question:
The transformer shown in Figure f is ideal. If resistor Y is removed, which of the following will happen?

(1) The primary current decreases.

(2) The secondary current decreases.

(3) The power dissipated by resistor X increases.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-408-8.reasoning:
The secondary voltage depends only on the primary voltage and is not affected by the secondary circuit.

If Y is removed, the resistance of the secondary circuit increases. Therefore, the secondary current decreases.

∴ (2) is correct.

By VpIp = VsIs, Ip decreases when Is decreases.

∴ (1) is correct.

The resistance RX of X is larger than the equivalent resistance RXY of X and Y.

Voltage VX across X before Y is removed

=Vs(RXYRXY + RZ)

Voltage VX′ across X after Y is removed

=Vs(RXRX + RZ) > VX

∴ The voltage across X increases after Y is removed.

By P =V2R, the power dissipated by resistor X increases.

∴ (3) is correct.
